title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): f: X -> S is a smooth morphism of complex analytic spaces. The omega_i are closed relative holomorphic 1-forms on X/S, and a, b are sections of f whose values lie in the same connected component of each fibre. Locally on S one chooses a continuously varying path C_s from a(s) to b(s). The incomplete integral I(s) = ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_s is holomorphic in s. Changing the path changes I by a period ∫_{Z_s} omega_s over a continuous family of 1-cycles Z_s.

This page: for a formal expression mu = (D_i, omega_i)_{i in I}, with D_i differential operators on S, the function sum_i D_i ∫_a^b omega_i depends on the path choice only modulo expressions (3) sum_i D_i ∫_{Z_s} omega_i. Grothendieck defines mu to be a 'Picard–Fuchs equation on X/S' if (3) vanishes for every continuous family of 1-cycles over every open of S. For such mu and any local sections a, b, the expression (4) mu(a,b) = sum_i D_i ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_i is a well-defined holomorphic function on S. It satisfies the cocycle (Chasles) relation (5) mu(a,b) + mu(b,c) = mu(a,c). The page ends by asking for a manageable infinitesimal criterion, rather than a global one, for mu to be Picard–Fuchs.

Next page: the criterion is formulated in Phi = f_*(closed relative 1-forms) / d f_*(O_X). Phi carries a natural integrable (Gauss–Manin) connection defined via the Cartan formula. The sufficient condition is (7) sum D_i omega_i = 0 in Phi. Then one lifts the D_i to operators on Omega^*_X commuting with d_{X/S}, and forms the closed form omega-bar = sum alpha_{D_i} omega_i. Presumably the conclusion is that mu(a,b) = phi(b) - phi(a) for a function phi with omega-bar = d_{X/S} phi, up to endpoint correction terms.

In modern terms: a Picard–Fuchs operator annihilates the periods of a family. Applied to an incomplete (abelian) integral from a to b, it yields a holomorphic (in the algebraic case, algebraic or rational) function of the endpoints. This function is additive in the endpoints, hence a homomorphism from sections, or from the relative Albanese/Jacobian, to O_S. This is exactly the Manin map (Manin's 'theorem of the kernel', 1963), used in Manin's proof of Mordell over function fields. The page is a careful general formalisation of that construction for arbitrary smooth analytic families of open varieties.
errors: Phi = f_*(Z Omega^1_{X/S}) / d f_* O_X agrees with the relative de Rham H^1 (and hence carries the Gauss–Manin connection as stated) only under hypotheses: e.g. Stein or affine fibres, or after passing to hypercohomology in the proper case. In general global closed forms modulo global exact forms do not compute R^1 f_* C ⊗ O_S. The next page's marginal note ('connexion sur Phi seulement si X->S est lisse') shows Grothendieck was aware of hypotheses.

Differentiating ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_s produces endpoint terms <omega, b'> - <omega, a'> besides the Gauss–Manin derivative. Hence mu(a,b) is not ∫_a^b of sum D_i omega_i, and the vanishing in (7) does not make mu(a,b) zero. This is fine and intended (it is the source of the nontrivial Manin map), but the step needs care with the lifts D-bar_i.
Minor: (7) is only claimed sufficient. Necessity fails in general without knowing that cycles generate the dual of Phi.

ideas.what: Definition of a Picard–Fuchs equation as a tuple (D_i, omega_i) annihilating all periods over continuous families of 1-cycles
ideas.modern_name: Picard–Fuchs operator / element of the D_S-module kernel of the Gauss–Manin system
ideas.where_published: Gauss–Manin connection is in Katz–Oda and Katz's work inspired by Grothendieck's 1966 letter/IHES 'crystals' ideas; not this formulation

ideas.what: Applying a Picard–Fuchs operator to an incomplete integral between two sections gives a well-defined holomorphic function, additive in the endpoints
ideas.modern_name: Manin map / Manin's theorem of the kernel
ideas.usually_credited_to: Yu. Manin 1963; revisited by Coleman 1990, Chai 1991, Bertrand

ideas.what: Infinitesimal criterion: sum D_i omega_i = 0 in Phi with its Gauss–Manin connection (via Cartan formula), with lifts of D_i to operators on Omega_X
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection on relative de Rham cohomology; Katz–Oda construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck worked out (probably c. 1972) a general analytic formalisation of Manin's kernel construction for arbitrary smooth families with closed relative 1-forms, not necessarily proper: periods over continuous families of cycles, incomplete integrals between sections, and an endpoint cocycle relation. This is an unrecorded engagement with Manin's function-field Mordell method, which later turned out to have a gap repaired by Coleman (1990). It is not a new result.
missed.quote: Disons que μ = (D_i, ω_i)_{i∈I} [est une] équation de Picard-Fuchs sur X/S. Alors pour deux sections loc. quelc. a, b de X/S, l'expression μ(a,b) = Σ D_is ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} ω_is est bien déterminée ... μ(a,b)+μ(b,c)=μ(a,c)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck's interest in the Manin map and Gauss–Manin formalism for open fibres. The mathematics itself is in the literature (Manin, Coleman, Chai, Bertrand).

deep.surprise_reason: A clean general set-up of the Manin map via Picard–Fuchs equations on incomplete integrals. The mathematics is known (Manin 1963, later Coleman/Chai). The only point of note is the documentation of Grothendieck's treatment, not a new result or connection.

'quelle que soit la famille continue sur Z_s de 1-cycles [?] sur un ouvert de S' should read roughly 'quelle que soit la famille continue Z_s de 1-cycles ... sur un ouvert de S'. The next line begins with a word like 'Disons' ('Disons que μ = (D_i, ω_i)_{i∈I} est une équation de Picard-Fuchs'). The phrase 'définit une' is struck and replaced by 'équation'.
The struck '(NB) Le fait que Z_s est un 1-cycle permet' is correctly marked deleted. The crossed-out material after (3) appears to be an attempted 'Σ D_is ∫_{Z_s} ω_is'.
'Bien sûr on aura' is followed by (5). On the same line as (5), at right, 'Les formes différentielles' (cut off, 'diffé-') begins the text.
The struck phrase near the bottom reads approximately 'telle [qu'elle soit] infinitésimale, et non plus globale' and is struck through.
